source.text: וַיִּקְרָ֖א אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֑ה וַיְדַבֵּ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֵלָ֔יו מֵאֹ֥הֶל מוֹעֵ֖ד לֵאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And he called to Moses, and spoke Yahweh to him from [the] tent of meeting, saying,

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} called to Moses, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to him from the tent of meeting, saying,
en.B: From the tent of meeting {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} called to Moses and spoke to him. He said,
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} called to Moses from the meeting tent. He said to him,

decisions.choice: the tent of meeting: the tent where God met with Moses and with Israel
decisions.reason: This is the tent Moses set up in Exodus 40, also called the dwelling place (the tabernacle). "Meeting" comes from a verb for meeting at a set time or place: God said, "There I will meet with you" (Exodus 25:22; 29:42-43). It is the place from which God speaks and where offerings are brought, at its entrance (verse 3).

decisions.choice: he called to Moses: Yahweh speaks from the tent that his glory has just filled
decisions.reason: Exodus ends with the glory of Yahweh filling the tent, so that Moses could not go in (Exodus 40:34-35). Leviticus begins with God calling to Moses from inside it. The first verb has no subject, which is supplied by "Yahweh" in the next clause. The book's Hebrew name is its first word, "And he called".

decisions.choice: the meeting tent
decisions.reason: Readable says "the meeting tent", which a young reader can follow more easily than "tent of meeting". Literal and Balanced keep "the tent of meeting".

decisions.choice: He said
decisions.reason: "Saying" introduces God's words. Balanced and Readable turn it into "He said" and put "from the tent" where it reads naturally.

source.text: דַּבֵּ֞ר אֶל־בְּנֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵהֶ֔ם אָדָ֗ם כִּֽי־יַקְרִ֥יב מִכֶּ֛ם קָרְבָּ֖ן לַֽיהוָ֑ה מִן־הַבְּהֵמָ֗ה מִן־הַבָּקָר֙ וּמִן־הַצֹּ֔אן תַּקְרִ֖יבוּ אֶת־קָרְבַּנְכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Speak to [the] sons of Israel and say to them, [a] person when he brings near from you [an] offering to Yahweh, from the livestock, from the herd and from the flock you will bring near your offering.

en.L: "Speak to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel and say to them, 'When anyone among you brings near an offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, from the livestock, from the herd and from the flock, you shall bring near your offering.
en.B: "Speak to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} and tell them: 'If one of you brings an animal to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as an offering, it is to come from the herd or from the flock.
en.R: "Tell the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}: 'When you bring an animal as an offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, it must be one of your cattle, sheep or goats.

decisions.choice: offering: something brought near to God
decisions.reason: The noun comes from the verb "bring near", and the verse uses both: "when anyone brings near an offering ... you shall bring near your offering". It is the general word for whatever is presented to God: animals (chapters 1 and 3), grain (2:1) and gifts for the sanctuary (Numbers 7:3). By it a worshiper comes near to God.

decisions.choice: anyone: any human being, man or woman
decisions.reason: The word is the general word for a human being, not the word for a male. The laws that follow are for whoever brings an offering; a woman also brings a burnt offering after childbirth (12:6).

decisions.choice: the livestock, the herd, the flock: domestic animals only
decisions.reason: "Livestock" is then narrowed to the herd (cattle, verse 3) and the flock (sheep and goats, verse 10). Wild animals are not offered. Birds, allowed in verse 14, are the one exception.

decisions.choice: brings / bring
decisions.reason: "Bring near" is kept at Literal to show the link between the verb and the noun "offering". Balanced and Readable say "bring" or "present". Readable lists the animals of the herd and flock: cattle, sheep and goats.

decisions.choice: anyone / one of you / you
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word is already inclusive, so no gender setting is needed. In the laws that follow the Hebrew says "he" for this person; Literal keeps "he", Balanced uses "the worshiper", "they" or a passive, and Readable speaks to the reader as "you", as this verse already does.

source.text: אִם־עֹלָ֤ה קָרְבָּנוֹ֙ מִן־הַבָּקָ֔ר זָכָ֥ר תָּמִ֖ים יַקְרִיבֶ֑נּוּ אֶל־פֶּ֝תַחאֹ֤הֶל מוֹעֵד֙ יַקְרִ֣יב אֹת֔וֹ לִרְצֹנ֖וֹ לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: If [a] burnt offering [is] his offering from the herd, [a] male unblemished he will bring near it; to [the] entrance of [the] tent of meeting he will bring near it, for his acceptance before Yahweh.

en.L: If his offering [is] a burnt offering from the herd, he shall bring near a male, unblemished; to the entrance of the tent of meeting he shall bring it near, for his acceptance before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: A burnt offering from the herd must be a male without defect. It is to be brought to the entrance of the tent of meeting, so that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will accept the one who offers it.
en.R: If you bring a burnt offering from your cattle, it must be a male with nothing wrong with it. Bring it to the entrance of the meeting tent. Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will accept you.

decisions.choice: burnt offering: an offering that goes up whole in smoke
decisions.reason: The word comes from the verb "go up". All of the animal except its skin (7:8) goes up in smoke on the altar (verse 9), and nothing is eaten. It was offered every morning and evening (Exodus 29:38-42), and could be brought by anyone as a gift, a vow or a plea to God.

decisions.choice: unblemished: whole, with no physical defect
decisions.reason: The word means complete or whole. Of an animal it means one with no defect: 22:17-25 lists what makes an animal unfit, such as blindness, injury or deformity. God is to be given what is whole, not what is damaged (Malachi 1:8). The same word describes people who are blameless (Genesis 6:9; 17:1).

decisions.choice: for his acceptance: so that the worshiper is accepted before Yahweh
decisions.reason: "His" most likely refers to the worshiper, as verse 4 says: "it will be accepted for him" (compare 22:19-21). An older reading takes it as "of his own free will", but the word is used in these laws for God's acceptance of the offerer.

decisions.choice: so that the LORD will accept the one who offers it
decisions.reason: Balanced turns "for his acceptance before the LORD" into a clause with the LORD as the subject, and uses passives so that it does not need "he" for a worshiper who may be a man or a woman.

decisions.choice: with nothing wrong with it; you
decisions.reason: Readable explains "unblemished" in common words and speaks to the reader directly, as in verse 2.

source.text: וְסָמַ֣ךְ יָד֔וֹ עַ֖ל רֹ֣אשׁ הָעֹלָ֑ה וְנִרְצָ֥ה ל֖וֹ לְכַפֵּ֥ר עָלָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And he will lean his hand on [the] head of the burnt offering, and it will be accepted for him to make atonement for him.

en.L: And he shall lean his hand on the head of the burnt offering, and it will be accepted for him, to make atonement for him.
en.B: The worshiper is to lay their hand on the head of the burnt offering, which will then be accepted for them and make atonement for them.
en.R: Put your hand on the head of the animal. Then it will be accepted for you, to make atonement for you.

decisions.choice: lean his hand on the head: a gesture marking the animal as the worshiper's own offering
alternatives: a sign that the worshiper's sin passes to the animal
decisions.reason: The verb means to press or lean, not merely to touch. The same act is done for the peace offering (3:2) and the sin offering (4:4). The text does not explain it here. At least it shows that this animal is the worshiper's own and is given on that person's behalf. In 16:21 Aaron leans both hands on the goat's head while confessing Israel's sins over it, and Moses commissions Joshua with the same gesture (Numbers 27:18-23).

decisions.choice: make atonement: put right what stands between the worshiper and God
decisions.reason: The verb is used throughout Leviticus for what the priest does with an offering on someone's behalf. It covers wiping away the stain of sin and impurity (16:30), and paying a ransom for a life (Exodus 30:12-16); the blood given on the altar is the means (17:11). Even the burnt offering, which is not tied to one particular sin, makes atonement: it reconciles the worshiper to God.

decisions.choice: it will be accepted for him: God accepts the offering on the worshiper's behalf
decisions.reason: The same verb is used in 7:18 and 22:23-27 of an offering God accepts or refuses.

decisions.choice: lay (Balanced); put (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal says "lean", which is closer to the Hebrew verb. Balanced keeps the familiar "lay his hand on", with "their" for a worshiper who may be a man or a woman; Readable says "put".

source.text: וְשָׁחַ֛ט אֶת־בֶּ֥ן הַבָּקָ֖ר לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וְ֠הִקְרִיבוּ בְּנֵ֨י אַהֲרֹ֤ן הַֽכֹּֽהֲנִים֙ אֶת־הַדָּ֔ם וְזָרְק֨וּ אֶת־הַדָּ֤ם עַל־הַמִּזְבֵּ֨חַ֙ סָבִ֔יב אֲשֶׁר־פֶּ֖תַח אֹ֥הֶל מוֹעֵֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: And he will slaughter the son of the herd before Yahweh, and will bring near [the] sons of Aaron, the priests, the blood and throw the blood against the altar all around, which [is at the] entrance of [the] tent of meeting.

en.L: And he shall slaughter the young bull before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and the sons of Aaron, the priests, shall bring near the blood and throw the blood against the altar all around, which [is at] the entrance of the tent of meeting.
en.B: The one who brought the young bull is to slaughter it there before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Aaron's sons, the priests, are then to present the blood and splash it on every side of the altar that stands at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
en.R: Then you must kill the young bull there in front of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Aaron's sons, the priests, will bring the blood. They will splash it on all sides of the altar at the entrance of the meeting tent.

decisions.choice: the son of the herd: a young bull
decisions.reason: "Son of the herd" means a young animal of the cattle, here the male of verse 3.

decisions.choice: the worshiper slaughters; the priests handle the blood
decisions.reason: The one who brings the animal kills it; the priests' work begins with the blood. Only they serve at the altar, the bronze altar of burnt offering that stood in the courtyard before the entrance of the tent (Exodus 27:1-8; 40:6, 29).

decisions.choice: throw the blood against the altar all around: splash it on every side
decisions.reason: The verb means to throw or dash a liquid in quantity, from a bowl; the word for the priests' bowls comes from it (Exodus 27:3). It is different from "sprinkle", done with a finger (4:6). "All around" means that the blood reached every side of the altar.

decisions.choice: splash
decisions.reason: Literal says "throw"; Balanced and Readable say "splash", which describes the action and keeps it distinct from "sprinkle".

decisions.choice: The one who brought the young bull
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "he". Balanced names the worshiper so that the reader does not take "he" for the priest, who is first mentioned later in the verse.

records.literal_gloss: And he will skin the burnt offering and cut it into its pieces.

en.L: And he shall skin the burnt offering and cut it into its pieces.
en.B: The worshiper is then to skin the burnt offering and cut it up into its parts.
en.R: Then you must take off the animal's skin and cut the animal into its parts.

decisions.choice: skin it and cut it into its pieces
decisions.reason: The skin of a burnt offering goes to the priest who offers it (7:8). "Its pieces" are the natural parts of the body, named in verse 8: the head, the fat and the rest.

decisions.choice: he will skin: most likely the worshiper, as in verse 5
decisions.reason: The subject is not named. It is most naturally the one who slaughtered the animal in verse 5. In 2 Chronicles 29:34 it is the priests, helped by the Levites, who skin the burnt offerings.

source.text: וְ֠נָתְנוּ בְּנֵ֨י אַהֲרֹ֧ן הַכֹּהֵ֛ן אֵ֖שׁ עַל־הַמִּזְבֵּ֑חַ וְעָרְכ֥וּ עֵצִ֖ים עַל־הָאֵֽשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: And will put [the] sons of Aaron the priest fire on the altar and arrange wood on the fire.

en.L: And the sons of Aaron the priest shall put fire on the altar and arrange wood on the fire.
en.B: The sons of Aaron the priest are to put fire on the altar and lay wood in order on the fire.
en.R: The sons of Aaron the priest will start a fire on the altar and stack wood on it.

decisions.choice: Aaron the priest: here "priest" is singular
decisions.reason: In the Hebrew text "the priest" here is singular and names Aaron, whose sons do the work, whereas verses 5 and 8 say "Aaron's sons, the priests".

decisions.choice: put fire on the altar and arrange wood
decisions.reason: The law assumes a fire on the altar. Later it is commanded that the fire be kept burning and never go out (6:5-6), and when the priests first offered, fire came out from before Yahweh and consumed the offering (9:24).

decisions.choice: start a fire ... stack wood
decisions.reason: Readable says "start a fire" for "put fire" and "stack" for "arrange".

source.text: וְעָרְכ֗וּ בְּנֵ֤י אַהֲרֹן֙ הַכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים אֵ֚ת הַנְּתָחִ֔ים אֶת־הָרֹ֖אשׁ וְאֶת־הַפָּ֑דֶר עַל־הָעֵצִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל־הָאֵ֔שׁ אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־הַמִּזְבֵּֽחַ׃

records.literal_gloss: And will arrange [the] sons of Aaron, the priests, the pieces, the head and the suet, on the wood which [is] on the fire which [is] on the altar.

en.L: And the sons of Aaron, the priests, shall arrange the pieces, the head and the suet on the wood that [is] on the fire that [is] on the altar.
en.B: Aaron's sons, the priests, are to set out the pieces on the burning wood of the altar, along with the head and the suet.
en.R: Then they will place the pieces, the head and the fat on the burning wood on the altar.

decisions.choice: suet: hard fat
decisions.reason: This word for fat occurs only here, in verse 12 and in 8:20. It is probably the hard fat around the inner organs, but it is a different word from "the fat" of chapter 3, and its exact sense is not certain.

decisions.choice: arrange ... on the wood on the fire on the altar
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for the wood in verse 7: things are laid out in order. The chain "wood ... fire ... altar" pictures the offering laid on the fire burning on the altar.

decisions.choice: the fat
decisions.reason: Readable says "the fat" for the rare word Literal and Balanced render "suet".

source.text: וְקִרְבּ֥וֹ וּכְרָעָ֖יו יִרְחַ֣ץ בַּמָּ֑יִם וְהִקְטִ֨יר הַכֹּהֵ֤ן אֶת־הַכֹּל֙ הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חָה עֹלָ֛ה אִשֵּׁ֥ה רֵֽיחַ־נִיח֖וֹחַ לַֽיהוָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And its entrails and its legs he will wash with water, and will make smoke the priest the whole on the altar, [a] burnt offering, [a] fire offering, [an] odor of soothing to Yahweh.

en.L: And its entrails and its legs he shall wash with water, and the priest shall make the whole smoke on the altar, a burnt offering, an offering by fire, an aroma of soothing to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: The internal organs and the legs are to be washed with water, and the priest is to turn the whole animal into smoke on the altar. It is a burnt offering, a food offering, a soothing aroma to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: You must wash the inner organs and the legs with water. Then the priest must burn all of it on the altar. It is a burnt offering, a food offering burned on the fire, a smell that pleases {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: make smoke: turn into smoke on the altar
decisions.reason: The verb is not the ordinary word for burning. It means to make something go up as smoke, and it is used of incense as well (Exodus 30:7). The offering rises to God as smoke.

decisions.choice: fire offering: a gift presented to God, normally on the altar fire
decisions.reason: The word has long been linked with the word for fire, hence "an offering by fire". But it is also used of things that are not burned, such as the bread of the presence, which the priests eat (24:7-9), and the wine of a drink offering (Numbers 15:10). It may therefore mean a gift, or food, presented to God. In 3:11 it is called "food".

decisions.choice: an odor of soothing: a pleasing smell that God accepts
decisions.reason: The phrase first appears in Genesis 8:21, where God smells Noah's offering and promises never again to curse the ground. It says in human terms that God is pleased with the offering and accepts the worshiper. It does not mean that God needs food (Psalm 50:12-13).

decisions.choice: a food offering (Balanced); a food offering burned on the fire (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the traditional "an offering by fire". Balanced says "a food offering", which fits both senses noted above; Readable adds that it is burned on the fire.

decisions.choice: a smell that pleases the LORD
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "a soothing aroma" means.

decisions.choice: internal organs; turn into smoke
decisions.reason: Balanced says "internal organs" for "entrails" and "turn into smoke" for the verb "make smoke"; Readable says "burn".

source.text: וְאִם־מִן־הַצֹּ֨אן קָרְבָּנ֧וֹ מִן־הַכְּשָׂבִ֛ים א֥וֹ מִן־הָעִזִּ֖ים לְעֹלָ֑ה זָכָ֥ר תָּמִ֖ים יַקְרִיבֶֽנּוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And if from the flock [is] his offering, from the sheep or from the goats, for [a] burnt offering, [a] male unblemished he will bring near it.

en.L: And if his offering [is] from the flock, from the sheep or from the goats, for a burnt offering, he shall bring near a male, unblemished.
en.B: If the animal for the burnt offering comes from the flock, from the sheep or the goats, it must be a male without defect.
en.R: If you bring a sheep or a goat as a burnt offering, it must be a male. It must be healthy and perfect.

decisions.choice: the flock: sheep and goats
decisions.reason: "The flock" means the small livestock, sheep and goats together. The word for sheep here means young rams or lambs.

decisions.choice: the same rite for a smaller animal
decisions.reason: Verses 10-13 repeat the rite of verses 3-9 for a sheep or goat, and verses 14-17 for a bird. The law lets each worshiper give what they can (compare 5:7).

decisions.choice: healthy and perfect
decisions.reason: Readable explains "unblemished" in common words.

source.text: וְשָׁחַ֨ט אֹת֜וֹ עַ֣ל יֶ֧רֶךְ הַמִּזְבֵּ֛חַ צָפֹ֖נָה לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וְזָרְק֡וּ בְּנֵי֩ אַהֲרֹ֨ן הַכֹּהֲנִ֧ים אֶת־דָּמ֛וֹ עַל־הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ סָבִֽיב׃

records.literal_gloss: And he will slaughter it at [the] side of the altar northward before Yahweh, and will throw [the] sons of Aaron, the priests, its blood against the altar all around.

en.L: And he shall slaughter it at the side of the altar northward before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and the sons of Aaron, the priests, shall throw its blood against the altar all around.
en.B: It is to be slaughtered before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} on the north side of the altar, and Aaron's sons, the priests, are to splash its blood on every side of the altar.
en.R: You must kill it in front of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} on the north side of the altar. Aaron's sons, the priests, will splash its blood on all sides of the altar.

decisions.choice: the north side of the altar
decisions.reason: The text gives no reason. The east side held the place for the ashes (verse 16), and the place where burnt offerings are slaughtered is later the place for the sin and guilt offerings too (4:24; 6:18; 7:2).

decisions.choice: throw its blood against the altar all around
decisions.reason: As with the young bull (verse 5).

source.text: וְנִתַּ֤ח אֹתוֹ֙ לִנְתָחָ֔יו וְאֶת־רֹאשׁ֖וֹ וְאֶת־פִּדְר֑וֹ וְעָרַ֤ךְ הַכֹּהֵן֙ אֹתָ֔ם עַל־הָֽעֵצִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל־הָאֵ֔שׁ אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל־הַמִּזְבֵּֽחַ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he will cut it into its pieces, and its head and its suet, and will arrange the priest them on the wood which [is] on the fire which [is] on the altar.

en.L: And he shall cut it into its pieces, with its head and its suet, and the priest shall arrange them on the wood that [is] on the fire that [is] on the altar.
en.B: It is to be cut into its pieces, and the priest is to set them out, with the head and the suet, on the burning wood of the altar.
en.R: Then you must cut it into pieces. The priest will place the pieces, the head and the fat on the burning wood on the altar.

decisions.choice: and its head and its suet: laid out with the pieces
decisions.reason: The head and the suet are named loosely after "its pieces"; they are cut off and arranged with the rest, as in verse 8. See the note on "suet" there.

source.text: וְהַקֶּ֥רֶב וְהַכְּרָעַ֖יִם יִרְחַ֣ץ בַּמָּ֑יִם וְהִקְרִ֨יב הַכֹּהֵ֤ן אֶת־הַכֹּל֙ וְהִקְטִ֣יר הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חָה עֹלָ֣ה ה֗וּא אִשֵּׁ֛ה רֵ֥יחַ נִיחֹ֖חַ לַיהוָֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And the entrails and the legs he will wash with water, and will bring near the priest the whole and make [it] smoke on the altar; [a] burnt offering it [is], [a] fire offering, [an] odor of soothing to Yahweh.

en.L: And the entrails and the legs he shall wash with water, and the priest shall bring near the whole and make [it] smoke on the altar; it [is] a burnt offering, an offering by fire, an aroma of soothing to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: The internal organs and the legs are to be washed with water. The priest is to present all of it and turn it into smoke on the altar. It is a burnt offering, a food offering, a soothing aroma to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: You must wash the inner organs and the legs with water. The priest will offer all of it and burn it on the altar. It is a burnt offering, a food offering burned on the fire, a smell that pleases {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: it is a burnt offering: the closing formula
decisions.reason: The same words close the rite for cattle (verse 9) and for birds (verse 17). See the notes at verse 9.

source.text: וְאִ֧ם מִן־הָע֛וֹף עֹלָ֥ה קָרְבָּנ֖וֹ לַֽיהוָ֑ה וְהִקְרִ֣יב מִן־הַתֹּרִ֗ים א֛וֹ מִן־בְּנֵ֥י הַיּוֹנָ֖ה אֶת־קָרְבָּנֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And if from the bird[s] [is a] burnt offering, his offering to Yahweh, then he will bring near from the turtledoves or from [the] sons of the dove his offering.

en.L: And if his offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] a burnt offering from the birds, then he shall bring near his offering from the turtledoves or from the young pigeons.
en.B: If someone's burnt offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is a bird, they are to bring a turtledove or a young pigeon.
en.R: If you offer a bird as a burnt offering to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, choose a dove or a young pigeon.

decisions.choice: turtledoves or young pigeons
decisions.reason: The turtledove is a small wild dove; "sons of the dove" means young doves or pigeons, which were kept and bred.

decisions.choice: a bird: the offering of someone who cannot afford a larger animal
decisions.reason: Birds are allowed for those who cannot afford a lamb (5:7; 12:8). Mary and Joseph offered "a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons" (Luke 2:24).

decisions.choice: a dove
decisions.reason: Readable says "dove" for "turtledove".

source.text: וְהִקְרִיב֤וֹ הַכֹּהֵן֙ אֶל־הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ וּמָלַק֙ אֶת־רֹאשׁ֔וֹ וְהִקְטִ֖יר הַמִּזְבֵּ֑חָה וְנִמְצָ֣ה דָמ֔וֹ עַ֖ל קִ֥יר הַמִּזְבֵּֽחַ׃

records.literal_gloss: And will bring it near the priest to the altar and nip off its head and make [it] smoke on the altar, and will be drained out its blood on [the] wall of the altar.

en.L: And the priest shall bring it near to the altar and nip off its head and make [it] smoke on the altar, and its blood shall be drained out on the side of the altar.
en.B: The priest is to take it to the altar. He is to nip off its head and turn the head into smoke on the altar, and the bird's blood is to be squeezed out against the altar's side.
en.R: The priest will take the bird to the altar. He will pull off its head and burn the head on the altar. Then he will let its blood drain out on the side of the altar.

decisions.choice: nip off: pinch off with the fingers
decisions.reason: The verb occurs only here and in 5:8, where the head of a bird for a sin offering is nipped but not severed. Here the head is removed and burned.

decisions.choice: its blood will be drained out on the side of the altar
decisions.reason: A bird has too little blood to splash, as is done with cattle and sheep (verses 5, 11). Instead it is squeezed or drained out against the altar's side.

decisions.choice: make it smoke: the head
decisions.reason: The verse may tell the whole rite in short and then add details. Most simply, the head is burned now and the body after verses 16-17.

decisions.choice: the head
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say that what is burned here is the head.

source.text: וְהֵסִ֥יר אֶת־מֻרְאָת֖וֹ בְּנֹצָתָ֑הּ וְהִשְׁלִ֨יךְ אֹתָ֜הּ אֵ֤צֶל הַמִּזְבֵּ֨חַ֙ קֵ֔דְמָה אֶל־מְק֖וֹם הַדָּֽשֶׁן׃

records.literal_gloss: And he will remove its crop with its feathers and throw it beside the altar eastward, to [the] place of the fatty ashes.

en.L: And he shall remove its crop with its feathers and throw it beside the altar, eastward, to the place of the fatty ashes.
en.B: He is to take out its crop along with its feathers and throw it down on the east side of the altar, at the place for the ashes.
en.R: He will remove the bird's crop and its feathers. He will throw them on the east side of the altar, where the ashes are piled.

decisions.choice: its crop: the pouch in a bird's throat where food is stored
decisions.reason: The word occurs only here. It most likely means the crop, the part where a bird holds the food it has eaten.

decisions.choice: with its feathers
decisions.reason: The word means feathers or plumage elsewhere (Ezekiel 17:3, 7; Job 39:13). Another reading, "with its contents", takes it from a different root and means the food in the crop.

decisions.choice: the fatty ashes: ash soaked with the fat of the offerings
decisions.reason: The word means fatness, and here the ashes from the altar, full of burned fat. They were put by the altar on the east side and later carried outside the camp to a clean place (4:12; 6:3-4).

decisions.choice: the ashes
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "the fatty ashes"; Balanced and Readable say "the ashes".

source.text: וְשִׁסַּ֨ע אֹת֣וֹ בִכְנָפָיו֮ לֹ֣א יַבְדִּיל֒ וְהִקְטִ֨יר אֹת֤וֹ הַכֹּהֵן֙ הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חָה עַל־הָעֵצִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל־הָאֵ֑שׁ עֹלָ֣ה ה֗וּא אִשֵּׁ֛ה רֵ֥יחַ נִיחֹ֖חַ לַיהוָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And he will tear it open by its wings, not he will divide [it], and will make smoke it the priest on the altar, on the wood which [is] on the fire; [a] burnt offering it [is], [a] fire offering, [an] odor of soothing to Yahweh.

en.L: And he shall tear it open by its wings; he shall not divide [it]; and the priest shall make it smoke on the altar, on the wood that [is] on the fire; it [is] a burnt offering, an offering by fire, an aroma of soothing to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Taking it by the wings, he is to tear it open but not split it in two. Then the priest is to turn it into smoke on the altar, on the burning wood. It is a burnt offering, a food offering, a soothing aroma to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: He will hold it by its wings and tear it open, but not into two parts. Then the priest will burn it on the fire on the altar. It is a burnt offering, a food offering burned on the fire, a smell that pleases {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: tear it open by its wings but not divide it
decisions.reason: The bird is opened but left in one piece. Compare Genesis 15:10, where Abram cut the animals in two but did not divide the birds.

decisions.choice: a soothing aroma: the bird is as acceptable as the bull
decisions.reason: The same closing words are said of the bull (verse 9), the sheep or goat (verse 13) and the bird. The smallest offering, brought by someone who cannot afford more, pleases God as much as the largest.
